markdown_report:
The best first step remains a controlled history-intervention diagnostic adapter. At 0% progress, trustworthy measurements precede an unvalidated compatibility reranker. No benchmark improvement or predictive validity is claimed.

**Insights from the starting point.** First, training-position margins cannot establish final-position quality; diagnose the final valid representation separately. Second, raw margins depend on score scale, and mean embedding cosine does not uniquely identify collapse; retain precise definitions and add ranking measurements. Third, qualitative feedback suggests overweighted isolated purchases, but intent, ownership and simulator traits remain unobserved; interventions assess model dependence only.

**Insights from related work.** First, FCESR separates removal-based necessity from retention-based sufficiency [1]; neither establishes causal preferences. Second, recency research motivates matched temporal controls [2]; intervention size, positions and last-item treatment matter. Third, complementary recommendation distinguishes substitutes from complements [3]; lexical similarity cannot establish compatibility or redundancy. Fourth, sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons [4]; full-catalog diagnostics cannot replace pinned HR@10.

**Directions and framework.** Three axes organize the work: measurement reliability, history dependence and evidence-supported item relations. The framework remains observational probes → controlled interventions → optional model changes. Missing specifications remain unknown. Diagnose recurrence coverage before choosing exact repetition; use audited title/description TF-IDF similarity when histories contain unique items [5]. Neither proxy establishes sustained intent.

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of 10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Controlled history audit: 4/7/5.** Originality: targeted integration (+), established interventions (−). Potential: actionable hypotheses (+), unproven association with gains (−). Difficulty: existing hooks (+), padding, matching and catalog scoring require care (−). References: [1,2,4].
- **Recurrence-conditioned residual pooling: 5/7/5.** Blend SASRec’s final state with learned recurring-interest pooling. Originality: targeted combination (+), familiar machinery (−). Potential: sustained-interest modeling (+), lexical recurrence can encode boilerplate (−). Difficulty: small architecture change (+), predictor and adapter require updates (−). References: [2,5].
- **Explicit-conflict reranking: 4/6/7.** Penalize text-supported conflicts. Originality: evidence abstention (+), established reranking (−). Potential: concrete mismatch reduction (+), sparse specifications (−). Difficulty: simple scoring (+), reliable extraction is demanding (−). Reference: [3].

**Selected algorithm.** Freeze users, checkpoints, histories, eligible catalogs, seeds and tie-breaking. Preserve the last item for primary removal/retention probes; analyze its removal separately. Compare targeted changes with disjoint random controls matched on count, position/recency strata and popularity; report infeasible matches. Keep original-history exclusions fixed. Report overlap@10, signed and absolute rank displacement of original top-10 items, coverage and seeded-control variation. Cache baselines and batch scoring under a declared budget. Treat fixed-position masking and deletion/repacking separately; verify padding semantics, finite outputs and final-valid-index readout before masking. Restore model mode and mark empty samples unavailable. Preserve the separate twenty-user full-catalog panel. Prospectively test diagnostic usefulness across trials; select only by four-category macro validation HR@10, with paired user-bootstrap uncertainty.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13632; [2] https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722; [3] https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.16135; [4] https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/; [5] https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/feature_extraction.html#text-feature-extraction.

idea.description: Implement a mode-safe, controlled history-intervention audit through the existing DiagnosisProbe interface, retaining current metrics and adding final-position ranking measurements, recurrence coverage checks and explicit intervention validity controls.
idea.motivation: The qualitative diagnosis suggests unsupported broad associations and overweighted isolated interactions. Existing training-position margins cannot distinguish these hypotheses. Controlled interventions offer a feasible initial investigation without assuming latent user traits or unavailable product attributes. Their value for improving validation HR@10 remains a hypothesis to test prospectively.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device) and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Access the actual trained module through view.model; save and restore its training flag in a finally block. Preserve legacy measurements with precise definitions, sample counts and unavailable values for empty samples. Categories and review-derived measurements remain unavailable; never infer them from the illustrative schemas.

Use training histories only. Before selecting a recurrence probe, report per-category repeated-user fraction and duplicate-event fraction, defined as (history length minus number of unique items) divided by history length. Deduplication can eliminate exact recurrence; zero coverage does not establish absent recurring interests. If coverage is inadequate, use cross-item lexical recurrence from titles and descriptions. A reproducible initial proxy uses training-catalog TF-IDF word unigrams/bigrams, lowercase text, L2 normalization and cosine similarity. For each earlier history item, define recurrence as having another history item with cosine at least 0.5; audit threshold sensitivity at 0.4 and 0.6 without choosing thresholds from validation gains. Missing or empty text yields unavailable evidence. Inspect deterministic samples of matched titles across all categories and report metadata coverage and likely boilerplate/edition matches. Timestamps describe bursts and returns only when observed; do not impute missing times. These choices define a lexical proxy, not ownership, compatibility, true intent, diversity or conformity.

Freeze the checkpoint, original histories, category item catalogs, eligibility masks and candidate ordering. Use deterministic training-user samples with seed 42. Set a bounded initial protocol of up to 20 eligible users per category, one selected checkpoint, and five control seeds 42–46; report actual counts, runtime and coverage. Keep the native simulator's twenty users and their full-catalog recommendations as a separate exploratory panel. All audit computation consumes the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget.

For the primary earlier-history intervention, keep the original last interaction as a mandatory anchor. Target earlier exact-repeat positions or lexical-recurrence positions under the declared proxy. For removal controls, sample positions disjoint from the target set, matching target counts within joint relative-position quartile and training-item-popularity quartile strata. Both sets exclude the anchor. If observed timestamps support additional recency matching, declare those bins before running the audit. Report infeasible controls instead of reducing target size, relaxing strata or allowing overlap. For retention probes, retain the target set plus anchor, compared with matched control sets plus the same anchor; the anchor alone is exempt from disjointness. Report last-item removal separately. Optional shuffle probes preserve membership and use matched shuffle controls, distinguishing older-history shuffling with a fixed last item from full-history shuffling.

Keep every item in the original observed history excluded throughout all interventions, including deleted items. Cache baseline scores and score the same eligible full category catalog for every version, batching item scoring. Break score ties by ascending item ID. Define overlap@k as intersection size divided by k. For each original top-k item, signed rank displacement is intervened rank minus original rank; positive values indicate demotion. Report mean signed displacement and mean absolute displacement separately, along with targeted-minus-control differences and variation across control seeds. Users with fewer than k eligible items require an explicit reduced-k report and must not be silently combined with overlap@10. Compare deterministic reruns on a small frozen subset.

Use deletion followed by chronological repacking and left padding as the primary transformation. It changes surviving positions and spacing, which limits interpretation. Fixed-position masking is a distinct optional probe: first inspect the actual model's attention implementation. Zeroing embeddings alone does not exclude keys or eliminate positional and bias effects. Do not silently modify attention semantics for diagnosis. If the trained model cannot safely support internal padding, mark masking unavailable. Any padding-safe architecture change constitutes a new model trial and must update training, predictor writing and compatibility hooks consistently. A valid implementation excludes zero-valued keys at every layer, suppresses padded-query outputs and handles fully masked rows before softmax. PyTorch MultiheadAttention boolean True excludes attention, whereas functional SDPA boolean True allows it. Verify finite outputs; multiplying NaNs by zero is insufficient. Gather the greatest nonzero sequence index, not nonzero-count minus one. Exclude empty intervention histories and report coverage unless a fallback was explicitly specified in advance.

Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four category routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, single-GPU execution and artifacts beneath the trial directory. Respect the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200. This diagnostic alone requires no inference architecture change. Preserve the pinned evaluator, its users and candidates, and selection by equal-weight four-category validation HR@10. Full-catalog intervention scores and training-pair win rates answer different questions. Record diagnostic hypotheses before inspecting subsequent trial gains; evaluate their association with paired validation improvements across trials. A matched-budget comparison with unguided proposals is needed before claiming diagnostic-guided search is better. For model comparisons, bootstrap the same validation users for both models within each category, then average category differences equally. Report category effects, macro effect and interval; this captures user-sampling uncertainty, not seed variability or repeated-search optimism. Avoid tuning the proxy repeatedly on the small validation panel. No experiments or independent source verification were performed here.
idea.pseudocode:
def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
    model = self.view.model
    was_training = model.training
    try:
        model.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            metrics = existing_probes_with_counts_and_missingness(train_loader)
            recurrence_coverage = measure_recurrence_by_category(training_histories)
            proxy = frozen_exact_or_tfidf_proxy(recurrence_coverage)
            masking_supported = verify_existing_padding_and_readout_semantics(model)

            for category in ALL_FOUR_CATEGORIES:
                users = frozen_training_user_sample(category, limit=20, seed=42)
                for user in users:
                    original = training_history(user)
                    if not original:
                        record_ineligible(user, 'empty_original_history')
                        continue
                    anchor = last_position(original)
                    target = recurring_earlier_positions(original, proxy, exclude=anchor)
                    if not target:
                        record_ineligible(user, 'no_proxy_evidence')
                        continue
                    candidates = frozen_catalog_excluding_original_history(category, original)
                    baseline = cached_score_final_valid_state(original, candidates)
                    controls = []
                    for seed in range(42, 47):
                        control = sample_disjoint_matched_positions(
                            original, target, seed=seed, exclude=anchor,
                            match_joint_position_and_popularity_strata=True)
                        if control is None:
                            record_infeasible_match(user, seed)
                        else:
                            controls.append(control)
                    if not controls:
                        continue

                    operations = ['delete_repack', 'retain_repack']
                    if masking_supported:
                        operations += ['mask_fixed_positions']
                    for operation in operations:
                        # Retention includes the mandatory shared last-item anchor.
                        targeted = intervene(original, target, operation, anchor=anchor)
                        target_scores = score_final_valid_state(targeted, candidates)
                        assert_finite(target_scores)
                        target_change = top10_overlap_and_rank_displacement(
                            baseline, target_scores, tie_break='ascending_item_id')
                        control_changes = []
                        for positions in controls:
                            altered = intervene(original, positions, operation, anchor=anchor)
                            scores = score_final_valid_state(altered, candidates)
                            assert_finite(scores)
                            control_changes.append(top10_overlap_and_rank_displacement(
                                baseline, scores, tie_break='ascending_item_id'))
                        record_paired_differences(target_change, control_changes)

            verify_deterministic_rerun_on_frozen_subset()
            metrics.update(summarize_by_category_with_coverage_and_control_variation())
            return metrics, metric_definitions
    finally:
        model.train(was_training)

# Prospective search record: log diagnostic hypotheses before subsequent validation gains.
# Selection remains external: mean of the four pinned validation HR@10 values.
# Compare models with paired within-category user bootstrap and equal category weights.

originality.positive: Integrates necessity, sufficiency, temporal controls, lexical-proxy coverage and benchmark-compatible diagnostic contracts into one targeted audit.
originality.negative: The intervention and ranking techniques are established; the contribution is careful integration rather than a new explanatory principle.

future_potential.positive: Can produce reproducible failure hypotheses and provide a foundation for testing whether diagnostic-guided model changes improve recommendation.
future_potential.negative: History sensitivity does not establish user intent, and no supplied evidence shows it predicts validation improvements; sparse proxy coverage may further limit usefulness.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses the existing sequence encoder, scoring hooks, public histories and lightweight TF-IDF without external weights.
code_difficulty.negative: Safe padding behavior, disjoint matched controls, full-catalog ranking, proxy audits and budget accounting make a robust implementation more demanding than the original rating of 3 suggested.

related_work.title: FCESR (2025)
contributions: The supplied summary distinguishes history-subset sufficiency from removal-based necessity.
limitations: Model dependence under intervention does not establish real-world causal preferences or predict benchmark gains.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias (2024)
contributions: The supplied summary motivates measuring excessive recency dependence in sequential recommendation.
limitations: Its reported findings do not establish that reducing recency improves this four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: Complementary Recommendation in E-commerce (2024)
contributions: Distinguishes substitution from complementarity and discusses asymmetric item relationships.
limitations: Does not supply missing compatibility specifications or establish user-level redundancy from purchases alone.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: The supplied summary documents that sampled evaluation can reverse model comparisons.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned benchmark; full-catalog diagnostic ordering must be interpreted separately.

related_work.title: Scikit-learn text feature extraction documentation
contributions: Documents reproducible TF-IDF representations that require no pretrained weights.
limitations: Lexical similarity can capture boilerplate or editions and does not establish user intent or compatibility.

related_work.title: PyTorch MultiheadAttention documentation
contributions: Specifies attention-mask and key-padding-mask behavior relevant to internal-padding interventions.
limitations: The actual trained architecture must be inspected; API documentation alone cannot establish that its masking and empty-row handling are correct.

related_work.title: PyTorch transformer building blocks guidance
contributions: Provides implementation guidance relevant to padding and attention behavior.
limitations: Correct adaptation still requires finite-output checks and consistency between training and inference.

related_work.title: Offline evaluation options
contributions: The supplied summary supports explicit evaluation protocols and paired statistical comparisons.
limitations: User-bootstrap uncertainty does not capture training-seed variability, repeated-search optimism or missing relevance judgments.

related_work.title: Beyond Top-1
contributions: The supplied summary motivates assessing counterfactual changes across top-k rankings.
limitations: Does not establish that top-k intervention sensitivity predicts HR@10 improvements.
